LESSON: READING 8.2.1 INTENSIVE READING

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade seven
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 8
Topic 8.2: Reading 8.2.1 Intensive Reading
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading 8.2.1 Intensive Reading, part of Strand 8 in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade seven ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: How can you identify the subject in a poem? 2. How are poems similar to songs?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. distinguish main ideas from supporting details from poems,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 8.2.1 Intensive Reading in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. use contextual clues to infer the meaning of words and phrases in a text,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 8.2.1 Intensive Reading in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. make connections between events in a poem and real life,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 8.2.1 Intensive Reading in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. summarise events in a poem

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 8.2.1 Intensive Reading in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

E. answer direct and inferential questions from poems,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 8.2.1 Intensive Reading in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

F. appreciate the role of reading comprehension in lifelong learning. ● In pairs, learners are guided to search online using digital device with assistive technology and offline the meaning of reading for interpretation and evaluation. ● In groups, learners are guided to discuss the meaning of reading for interpretation and evaluation. ● Learners are guided to visualise events, people, and places in poems. ● Learners are guided to predict events in poems. ● Learners are guided to utilise digital devices with assistive technology to check the meanings of words. ● Learners are guided to infer meanings of vocabulary based on contextual clues. 1. SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading 8.2.1 Intensive Reading together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Digital Literacy: A learner creates a word puzzle and share it online using digital devices.

● Critical thinking and problem-solving: A learner interprets and evaluates issues highlighted in poems and relate them

to real life.

Values:
Respect: A learner respects each other’s opinions as they work together.

Link to other subjects:

Social Studies and Business Studies require reading for interpretation and evaluation.

Suggested Learning Resources

Braille reading materials, digital devices with assistive technology like screen readers and braille display., sample poems.
